# The frozen data

Eight tiers, 28 MB, laid out along the chain that produced them:

```
Phase 14 pilot ──► Phase 15 training ──► Phase 15 held-out validation
                                              │
                                              ▼
                          Phase 16 fresh 24-cell confirmation
                                              │
                                              ▼
                        Phase 17 SWMDK application ──► Phase 18 crosswalk
```

| Tier | Files | Size |
|---|---:|---:|
| `empirical/` — 12 × 99,999 draws, artifacts, results | 52 | 18.6 MB |
| `confirmatory-raw/` — **86,400 raw replication rows** | 72 | 5.0 MB |
| `pilot/` | 23 | 4.5 MB |
| `confirmatory/`, `phase18/`, `design/`, `development/`, `validation/` | 60 | 0.2 MB |

Full column documentation: `data-frozen/CODEBOOK.md`.

## Reading it

```r
source("common/R/paths.R"); source("common/R/io.R")

raw   <- read_confirmatory_raw()   # 86,400 rows, binds all 24 gzipped files
draws <- read_draws(task = 1)      # 99,999 draws from P17-T01
swmdk <- read_swmdk()              # from mokken, digest asserted on every load
```

`verification/verify_numeric_basis.R` validates the complete raw layer: all 24
Phase 16 cells, all 12 Phase 17 draw streams, their manifests and receipts,
batch/draw identities, and their locked summaries. It is run by the cold-start
rehearsal and is independent of the exhibit builder.

::: {.callout-warning}
Never hand a `.gz` path to `data.table::fread()` — it decompresses in place and
mutates the frozen snapshot. The readers open `gzfile()` connections.
:::

## The application data does not ship

`SWMDK` is distributed inside the `mokken` package:

```r
library(mokken); data(SWMDK)
```

### What was locked

The Phase 17 protocol recorded these facts **before** the application ran:

| | |
|---|---|
| `mokken` version at lock | 3.1.2 |
| SHA-256 of the object | `e1257ff16f821ef3…70797` |
| Respondents | 639 |
| Clusters (`classId`) | 30 |
| Cluster size range | 5 – 29 |
| Score support | 1 – 5 |

```r
digest::digest(SWMDK, algo = "sha256")
#> e1257ff16f821ef3cf6c5eed88a91ae2ffa5a067e12603f32c02660d47270797
```

The digest is of the **data frame as loaded**; `as.matrix(SWMDK)` gives a
different value, and `config.yml` records which one the lock means.

::: {.callout-important}
If the digest does not match, the `mokken` you have installed ships different
data from the one the application ran on. `read_swmdk()` stops with both
digests and both version numbers. **That is a finding about the data source**,
not something to work around — every application number in the paper is
conditional on this object.
:::

### Where SWMDK comes from

A documented subset of the Dutch COOL^5-18^ cohort study, with items from
Peetsma and Van der Veen and subset construction following Koopman et al.
(2022). None of it is the authors' to relicense.

## The confirmation raw tier

24 per-cell files, **86,400 rows**. Load-bearing, not archival:
`01_build_key_numbers.R` derives the 48-row all-cell summary from it and
cross-checks against the locked regular-cell artifact at 1e-12. That summary
feeds `tabF1_cells.tex` and `FigF1_cells.pdf`.

Selection: `candidate == TRUE` and `gamma_cluster == -1.5` gives 19,200 rows,
all with `invalid_fraction == 0` and `total_draws == 499`.

Each cell also ships a truth file, whose `minimum_internal_cdf_gap` column is
what the [archival-defect check](09-reproducibility.qmd#the-archival-defect)
reads.

## A note on paths inside the locked artifacts

Seventy-five shipped receipts record the project-relative path each file had in
the research tree — strings beginning `codebase/research/v4/cluster-polytomous/…`.

Those are **provenance, not dependencies**. The executable paths registered in
`provenance/runnable-code.csv` do not source, import, execute, or require that
tree. Verification is allowed to read copied receipts and archival code as
data—for example, to check digests and banners—so a package-wide string search
is not the boundary. The paths remain legible because editing locked evidence
would break its digests and defeat the point of shipping it.
